minutes.summary: The Stormwater Task Force reviewed corrected impervious-area data for several properties, discussed pursuing a non-binding straw poll (rather than a bylaw vote) at the fall town meeting to gauge support for funding stormwater work through a dedicated utility fee versus the operating budget, and reviewed a contractor's (CEI) ongoing GIS inventory of catch basins, manholes and outfalls. The group also worked out a draft abatement/credit structure for the eventual utility fee and set next steps: inviting the finance official to discuss a budget, confirming the warrant deadline with the Town Administrator, and possibly holding a short Zoom meeting in late August to meet that deadline.

Members drafted a phased abatement/credit schedule for a future stormwater utility fee.
GIS and assessor staff will re-inspect and correct impervious-area data for several properties.
Group plans to invite the finance official next meeting and may hold a short Zoom session in late August to meet the town meeting warrant deadline.

why_it_matters: This affects how stormwater infrastructure work gets paid for going forward -- through a new dedicated utility bill or through the existing property tax/operating budget.
The fall town meeting question is a straw poll to gauge preference, not a binding vote, so no funding change would take effect from it alone.
A future utility fee would include an abatement/credit option for properties, which could affect what an individual property owner eventually owes.
